notes:
ACCESS. williams-sonoma.com is behind Akamai. Direct curl_cffi is throttled rather than uniformly blocked: chrome/edge/firefox profiles always got HTTP 403 'Restricted Access', while safari15_5 / safari17_0 / safari17_2_ios / safari18_0_ios got 200s intermittently (403 bursts clear after a pause, so every fetch retries across those four profiles with backoff). r.jina.ai, which carried the prior Home-Decor pass, is now useless here: jina itself answers 200 but williams-sonoma.com returns 403 to jina's fetcher on every /shop/ path (the homepage still renders through it). translate.goog 408s, Googlebot-UA 403s, WebFetch 403s. robots.txt names no Anthropic/Claude agent and disallows no /shop/ or /api/ path used here. The Chrome extension route was also unavailable: williams-sonoma.com is not in its permitted-site list, so navigation there is refused and JS execution is denied.

TREE. The complete mega-menu came from the site's own nav API, /api/catalog/v1/category/categorytree/shop/data.json (found in header.a021b2ee.js). It types every node - supercat / header (clickableHeader = a menu grouping row) / subcat / topcat / linkcat - and marks hidden nodes secret:true. Furniture lives in exactly two supercats: 'Furniture' (/shop/home-furniture/) with the header groups Living Room Furniture, Dining & Kitchen Furniture, Bedroom Furniture and Home Office, and 'Outdoor' (/shop/home-outdoor/) with the header groups Outdoor Lounge Furniture and Outdoor Dining Furniture. I walked every other supercat too: Bath has no vanities or bath furniture (towels/robes/accessories only); Home Essentials' shelving, cabinet-storage and ladders/step-stools nodes are kitchen storage goods, not furniture; 'Shop Rooms'/'Shop By Room' are shop-the-look room pages; the 1258-URL shop-sitemap turned up no furniture slug outside these two departments.

QTY. Every qty is response.numFound from the PLP's own product feed, /api/catalog/v1/category/products/shop/<cat>/<subcat>/index.json?index=0 - the endpoint the storefront itself calls (WCMProductsEndpoint in shop.cd506c32.js). That is the exact number the rendered header shows: shop.js defines productCount() as state.shop.cat.response.numFound and productCountDisplay.displayText is 'Items', so the header string is literally '<numFound> Items'. The rendered header could not be read directly this session because the count is client-rendered and no JS-rendering route reached the site, so I validated the feed three ways. (1) Against the 2026-08-08 rendered-header values recorded in notes/52.md for 17 Home-Decor categories: 7 exact, the other 10 off by -1 to +4 and in BOTH directions (Floor Lamps 8=8, Mirrors 27=27, Picture Frames 20=20, Chandeliers 42->43, Table Lamps 38->37, Dinner Plates 100->104, Sconces 22->21). Two-directional drift over 11 days is normal catalogue churn - decisively unlike Constructor.io on this property, which the prior pass measured HIGHER on 15 of 15 disagreements. No Constructor number is used anywhere here. (2) Full enumeration: unique pids paged to the end equal numFound exactly on Dining Chairs (69), Chairs (44), Outdoor Chairs & Chaises (52) and Beds & Headboards (38), and 15 further categories returned their whole product set on a single page with docs == numFound. (3) Every count was read twice with identical results, the numbers differ per category (no site-wide constant), and the breadcrumbs API confirmed each URL resolves to the node I intended (no silent parent-serving).

SUM CHECKS. Living Room children 26+26+4+44+26+22+30 = 178 against the site's own 'All Living Room' 179. Dining & Kitchen children 211 against 'All Dining & Kitchen' 214. Bedroom children 77, plus the excluded Mattresses 36 = 113, against 'All Bedroom' 108. Outdoor Lounge children 123 against 'All Outdoor Lounge Furniture' 119; Outdoor Dining children 103 against 'All Outdoor Dining Furniture' 96 (the Sets nodes overlap their component nodes). All consistent.

EXCLUDED, and why. Mattresses (36) - bedding per the brief, and the Beds & Headboards node is kept separately. Dining Seat Cushions, Outdoor Furniture Cushions, Outdoor Furniture Covers - textiles/covers. Desk Accessories - desk objects. Umbrellas (7 nodes) and Umbrella Bases - shade accessories, not furniture. Patio Heaters & Fire Pit Tables - heating appliances. Outdoor Planters, Outdoor Lighting, Outdoor Pillows, Performance Rugs. Every 'All X' roll-up (All Living Room, All Dining & Kitchen, All Bedroom, All Home Office, All Outdoor Lounge Furniture, All Outdoor Dining Furniture, All Outdoor Furniture, All Outdoor Kitchen) per the parent-vs-children rule. All named collection branches (Sofa & Sectional Collections, Dining & Kitchen Furniture Collections, Bedroom Furniture Collections, Outdoor Collections and their ~80 per-collection child pages such as Valencia, Larnaca Teak, Pasadena), Outdoor Kitchens (a /pages/ landing whose children are brand collections), New Arrivals, Featured, Clearance/Sale, Quick Ship and In Stock & Ready to Ship (availability filters), Furniture by Color > Brass Furniture and All Wood Furniture (colour/material filters), Steelcase / Sanderson / Hill House (brand shops), Mondavi and Top-Collections pages, collection guides, design-school and home-tour pages, dining-table tools, and Fabric Swatches / Fabric by the Yard / Wood, Woven & Stone Swatches (materials and parts).

The whole 'Contract Grade' branch (All Contract Grade, Contract Grade Sectionals / Sofas / Lounge Chairs / Side Tables & Consoles / Dining Tables / Dining Chairs & Banquettes / Bar & Counter Stools / Bedroom / Office / Outdoor, 14 nodes under the editorial 'Design Resources' header) is excluded: these are feature-facet views of the same catalogue - the PLP state exposes the facet literally as features|multi-select|Features:("Contract Grade") - so they are filter pages over the rows already recorded, not separate categories. Flagging here in case the merge wants them.

DEDUPED / HIDDEN NODES. 'Console Tables & Media' in the Living Room column is a linkcat whose heroLink is /shop/home-furniture/sideboard-buffet-table, i.e. the same page as 'Console Tables, Sideboards & Buffets' under Dining - recorded once, under Dining. 'Kitchen Islands & Stools' (24, secret:true) duplicates 'Kitchen Islands & Carts' (22) and is dropped. 'Dining Sets' (/home-furniture/indoor-dining-set-perf-pair, secret:true) returns no product feed at all and is not in the sitemap, so it is dropped; the outdoor equivalent 'Outdoor Dining Sets' is live and is kept. 'All Outdoor Kitchen' (25) and 'Outdoor Combo' are secret:true. The one secret node I did keep is 'Entryway' (17) - it is indexed in the sitemap and has a real breadcrumb - and it carries a MANUAL REVIEW flag because it overlaps the product-type rows.

NAMING. Sub-category names are the site's own mega-menu node names. One variance worth noting: the node the menu calls 'Console Tables, Sideboards & Buffets' is titled 'Console Tables, Sideboards & Media Consoles' in the breadcrumb API; I kept the menu wording.
